land.text: northern Vietnam, which 'was militarily occupied by the Southern Han' before Ngô Quyền's dynasty (Ngô dynasty page; 'Third Era of Northern Domination')

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Southern Han row runs 911-979 and is the Chinese state that held Jiaozhi until the Ngô; the page names no Cliopatria shape.

land.text: the Hồ state's land, conquered by the Ming in 1407 (Hồ dynasty page: 'The Hồ dynasty was conquered by the Chinese Ming dynasty in 1407'); Cliopatria's Ming shape grows by about 133,000 km2 in 1407

successors.note: The Ming held the land as Jiaozhi until the Lê (le-dynasty, 1428/1429) recovered it. Cliopatria's Ngô row ends in 1406.

capitals.name: Cổ Loa
capitals.note: Ngô dynasty infobox: 'Capital: Cổ Loa' (no years). The twelve-warlords anarchy 965-968 broke the realm into 12 states.

capitals.name: Hoa Lư
capitals.note: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh 'relocated the capital to his home in Hoa Lư' in 968; still the capital of the Anterior Lê (infobox) until 1009; the Lý page gives 'Hoa Lư (1009-1010)'.

capitals.name: Thăng Long (Hanoi)
capitals.note: Lý Thái Tổ began moving the capital in 1010 to Đại La, renamed Thăng Long; Trần infobox: 'Thăng Long (1225-1397)'.

capitals.name: Tây Đô / Thanh Hóa (Western Capital)
capitals.note: Trần infobox: 'Thanh Hóa (temp) (1397-1400)'; the Hồ page gives 'Tây Đô' as capital without years and says Hồ Quý Ly 'had a new capital built'.

correction.text: shape unchanged; applies from 939 (Ngô Quyền's dynasty, northern Vietnam from Cổ Loa) instead of 947

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Ngô Quyền 'founded the dynasty: February 1 939' (infobox) but Cliopatria's first shape begins in 947. The 947 shape is used for 939-946 because the page gives no boundary; the area is Cliopatria's 62,155 km2. The page gives no area to compare.

62,155 km2: the delta plus Thanh-Nghệ. The page names no frontier. Not drawn: the anarchy of the 12 warlords (infobox 965; text 'in 966, the country was divided into 12 states'), which ends in 968 with Đinh Bộ Lĩnh; Cliopatria keeps one state through 969.

Unverified: pages silent. The area doubles to 135,575 km2 and the bounding box reaches 23.3 N and 103 E, i.e. the whole northern highland to today's frontier, including Cao Bằng and Lạng Sơn that the Lý-Song War page calls 'disputed' until 1082-1084. Treat the uplands as claimed and soft. The Đinh page (968-980) gives 'Hoa Lư', the 970-975 tributary status to the Song and no area.

135,575 km2 for 980-1055, the Anterior Lê of Lê Hoàn ('980-1009') and the first Lý decades. The Song attack of 980-981 was halted at Bạch Đằng and moved no border; the 982 Cham campaign is an occupation, not a shape change. The page gives no area to compare.
Years only: 1056-1068. The shape loses 1,400 km2 (1%) in 1056 with no event on the pages opened; the next shape is dated from the 1069 cession, not 1072.

Years only: 1069-1076. Rudravarman III 'had to sign a treaty with Lý Thánh Tông to cede three territories Địa Lí, Ma Linh and Bố Chính' (1069); the shape's southern edge moves from 17.77 N to 16.94 N (Quảng Bình, northern Quảng Trị). Cliopatria dates it 1072. The Song-held Quảng Nguyên of 1077-1081 and its return in 1082 are the new keyframes 1077 and 1082.

correction.text: the 1072 shape without Cao Bằng and Lạng Sơn, the Quảng Nguyên land the Song kept in 1077-1081

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1077-1081. After the 1077 withdrawal 'the Song kept five disputed regions of Quảng Nguyên', which 'now comprise most of modern Vietnam's Cao Bằng Province and Lạng Sơn Province'; in 1082 'Emperor Lý Nhân Tông returned Yong, Qin, and Lian prefectures' and the Song 'relinquished its control of four prefectures and a county, including Quảng Nguyên'. The Yong, Qin and Lian prefectures that Đại Việt held in these years are an occupation overlay, not territory.

New keyframe, 1082-1187: the 1072 shape again once the Song 'relinquished its control of ... Quảng Nguyên'; the 1084 talks at the Yongping garrison fixed the Quảng Nguyên-Guihua border, which 'exists largely unmodified to the present day'. Cliopatria's 1072 shape stands unchanged for these years.
140,583 km2 for 1188-1205; a 0.1% change from 1072 (bounding box edge 102.97 to 103.04 E), no event on the pages opened: boundary noise.
141,022 km2 (+0.3%); no event on the pages opened: boundary noise.
140,583 km2 (-0.3%); no event on the pages opened. The Lý fell to the Trần in 1225 without a border change (Lý page: 'Lý Chiêu Hoàng abdicates, cedes throne to Trần Cảnh: 1225').
140,529 km2: unchanged; no event on the pages opened.
140,362 km2: unchanged; no event on the pages opened.
140,444 km2: unchanged; the Mongol invasions of 1258, 1285 and 1287-88 left no territorial change (occupations of Thăng Long only, in the ledger).
Years only: 1294-1305. 'In 1306, the king of Champa, Chế Mân, offered Vietnam two Cham prefectures, Ô and Lý'; Cliopatria moves the border in 1314. The shape itself (140,280 km2) stands.

Years only: 1306-1362. The shape (152,278 km2, the maximum; southern edge 16.04 N, the Hải Vân line) is the land after Ô and Lý passed to the Trần, which the page dates 1306, not 1314. The Chế Bồng Nga raids 1371-1390 did not change it. The page gives no area to compare. Gazetteer cell check (not a page): the 35 cells the shape gains in 1314 all lie inside Cliopatria's Champa shape of 1313, in Thừa Thiên - Huế and Quảng Trị.

Unverified: page budget. The shape loses 19,000 km2 (to 133,419 km2) and its western edge moves from 103.04 E to 103.95 E, i.e. the westernmost uplands (today's Laos) leave in 1363, the year Cliopatria's Lan Xang row begins. The Trần page does not mention it; the ledger carries the loss at confidence 1. Cell check against the gazetteer (not a page): all 76 cells lost in 1363 lie inside Cliopatria's Lan Xang shape of 1363.
134,343 km2 (+0.7%); no event on the pages opened: boundary noise.
133,419 km2: back to the 1363 outline; no event on the pages opened.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1402 shape plus the 'large territory' ceded by Champa in 1402 (read as Quảng Nam, Đà Nẵng and Quảng Ngãi)

keyframe_review.note: Applies 1402-1405 with Quảng Nam and Quảng Ngãi added; in 1406 the shape stands unchanged (new keyframe 1406). 'In 1402 the army of the Hồ dynasty under general Đỗ Mãn made significant inroads against Champa, prompting the Champa king to cede large territory to Vietnam.' The page does not name the land; Quảng Nam and Quảng Ngãi (with Đà Nẵng) are read from the champa dossier, which cites the Champa-Đại Việt War page (the four regions Thăng, Hoa, Tư and Nghĩa). Cliopatria's shape does not move in 1402.

New keyframe, 1406 only. The land ceded in 1402 returns to Champa as the Hồ fall (champa dossier, from the Champa-Đại Việt War page: 'Four former territories gained by Hồ Hán Thương were returned to Champa'); the Hồ page gives only the Ming invasion of 11 May 1406. The Cliopatria shape of 1402 stands unchanged for 1406 and the land passes to the Ming in 1407.

region.text: Cổ Loa and northern Vietnam, formerly occupied by the Southern Han

ledger.note: 939: Ngô Quyền founds the Ngô dynasty at Cổ Loa, ending Southern Han rule. Infobox 'Ngô Quyền founded the dynasty: February 1 939'; 'a semi-independent Vietnamese dynasty from 939 to 968'; the Battle of Bạch Đằng was in December 938; 'northern Vietnam was militarily occupied by the Southern Han'. The page names the capital, not a boundary.

968: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh ends the Anarchy of the 12 Warlords and founds Đại Cồ Việt at Hoa Lư. Infobox 'Đinh Bộ Lĩnh ends the Anarchy of the 12 Warlords and establishes dynasty: 968'; the Ngô page has the country divided among 12 warlords in 965/966 (not drawn; Cliopatria keeps one shape). Same state, same colour (rule 2).
968: the capital moves from Cổ Loa to Hoa Lư. 'relocated the capital to his home in Hoa Lư'.
980: Lê Hoàn takes the throne after the murder of Đinh Bộ Lĩnh (October 979); the Anterior Lê rule Đại Cồ Việt (infobox 980-1009). Đinh page: 'General Lê Hoàn succeeded the throne: 980'.

region.text: northern Champa around Indrapura (Đồng Dương)

ledger.note: 982: Lê Đại Hành's army sacks Indrapura and defeats Champa. 'In 982, Lê Đại Hành began expeditions to Champa'; the Cham king Paramesvaravarman I was killed and 'the Cham capital Indrapura was sacked'. Hatched: the champa dossier (se-01-a) records the matching occupation of northern Champa; the page says the seized territory was 'merged into the country' but names no land.

region.text: Champa, whose 'new king ... agreed to be a vassal state'

ledger.note: 983: Champa becomes a vassal of Đại Cồ Việt. 'The new king of Champa agreed to be a vassal state of Đại Cồ Việt in 983.' The page names no extent; Champa as a whole is read.

region.text: northern Champa around Indrapura (Đồng Dương)

ledger.note: 989: the Vietnamese presence at Indrapura closes. Page silent: the Anterior Lê page gives no end for the occupation and does not mention 989; the year is the end of Lưu Kế Tông's reign (986-989) as read in the champa dossier, whose occupation_end 989 this pairs with.
1009: Lý Công Uẩn is crowned and the Lý dynasty replaces the Anterior Lê. 'Coronation of Lý Công Uẩn: 21 November 1009'; 'the court agreed to enthrone ... Lý Công Uẩn' (Anterior Lê page).
1010: Lý Thái Tổ moves the capital from Hoa Lư to Thăng Long. 'After a year of enthronement, in 1010, Lý Thái Tổ started to move the capital from Hoa Lư' to Đại La, renamed Thăng Long.
1054: Lý Thánh Tông changes the state name from Đại Cồ Việt to Đại Việt. Infobox 'Lý Thánh Tông changes the state name from Đại Cồ Việt to Đại Việt: 1054'.

region.text: Địa Lí, Ma Linh and Bố Chính: Quảng Bình and the northern part of Quảng Trị

ledger.note: 1069: Lý Thánh Tông takes three districts from Champa. 'Rudravarman III had to sign a treaty with Lý Thánh Tông to cede three territories Địa Lí, Ma Linh and Bố Chính', in the area of modern Quảng Bình and Quảng Trị; Cliopatria moves the border in 1072. The champa dossier carries the matching loss.

region.text: Champa, tributary since 983

ledger.note: 1069: Champa's first vassalage closes. Page silent on when Champa stopped paying tribute; the Lý page says only that Champa 'stopped paying tribute' before the 1069 campaign and 'had to restore the tributary system'. Closed at the 1069 war as a bridge; no tint is drawn after it because no page gives its span.

region.text: Qinzhou, Lianzhou and Yongzhou (present-day Nanning) prefectures

ledger.note: 1075: Lý Thường Kiệt invades the Song. 'In autumn 1075 a naval fleet commanded by Lý Thường Kiệt captured Qinzhou and Lianzhou prefectures'; Yongzhou (Nanning) was breached on 1 March 1076; in 1077 'Đại Việt kept the Yong, Qin, and Lian prefectures'. Hatched over Song land to 1082.

region.text: the approach to Thăng Long, where the Song 'nearly reached' the capital in 1077

ledger.note: 1076: a Song army of over 300,000 invades Đại Việt. 'in 1076 the Song led an army of over 300,000 to invade Đại Việt and by 1077 nearly reached Thăng Long'; the Battle of the Như Nguyệt River was in 1077. The page names no frontier; the zone is the approach to Thăng Long.

region.text: the approach to Thăng Long

ledger.note: 1077: Lý Thường Kiệt stops the Song at the Như Nguyệt River and offers peace. 'the Song commander Guo Kui agreed to withdraw his troops'.

region.text: the five disputed regions of Quảng Nguyên, most of modern Cao Bằng and Lạng Sơn

ledger.note: 1077: the Song keep Quảng Nguyên. 'The Song kept five disputed regions of Quảng Nguyên (renamed Shun'anzhou ...)', which 'now comprise most of modern Vietnam's Cao Bằng Province and Lạng Sơn Province'. The page calls them disputed, so the loss is a reading; the page's counts differ (five regions in 1077, four prefectures and a county in 1082).

region.text: Qinzhou, Lianzhou and Yongzhou prefectures

ledger.note: 1082: Đại Việt gives back Yong, Qin and Lian. 'Emperor Lý Nhân Tông of Đại Việt returned Yong, Qin, and Lian prefectures back to Song authorities, along with their prisoners of war.'

region.text: Quảng Nguyên and the other prefectures the Song relinquished

ledger.note: 1082: the Song return Quảng Nguyên. In exchange the Song 'relinquished its control of four prefectures and a county, including Quảng Nguyên'; the talks of 6 July to 8 August 1084 fixed the Quảng Nguyên-Guihua border.

region.text: Nghệ An, briefly seized in 1132, and the coast of Thanh Hóa

ledger.note: 1132: Suryavarman II and the Cham briefly seize Nghệ An. 'In 1132, he persuaded Cham king Jaya Indravarman III to join forces with him to attack Đại Việt, where they briefly seized Nghệ An and pillaged the coastal districts of Thanh Hoá'; the Khmer army of 20,000 had been 'routed in battle' at Nghệ An in 1128 after the Vietnamese refused tribute in 1127. The khmer-empire dossier records the same contest.

region.text: Nghệ An and the frontier between Angkor and Đại Việt

ledger.note: 1136: a Vietnamese force under Đỗ Anh Vũ counterattacks across Laos and the Cham make peace. 'In 1136, a Vietnamese force under Đỗ Anh Vũ counterattacked the Khmer Empire across modern-day Laos with 30,000 men, but later retreated'; the Cham 'made peace with the Vietnamese'. The page gives no treaty and no land change; it adds that the three provinces ceded in 1069 were 'probably returned to Cham influence' in 1131-1136, which no shape here draws.

1225: Trần Cảnh replaces the Lý. 'the new Trần dynasty was created on the first day of the twelfth lunar month (Gregorian: December 31) 1225'; the Lý page: 'Lý Chiêu Hoàng abdicates, cedes throne to Trần Cảnh: 1225'. The state keeps the name Đại Việt.

region.text: Thăng Long, held for nine days in 1258

ledger.note: 1258: the Mongols under Uriyangkhadai take Thăng Long for nine days. Battles on 17-22 January 1258; 'Uriyangkhadai left Thang Long after nine days to invade the Song dynasty'; 'the provinces around the capital were still under Vietnamese control'. The tributary relationship with the Mongol court began in 1258 (Yuan dossier).

region.text: Thăng Long

ledger.note: 1258: the Mongols leave Thăng Long after nine days (the page gives no calendar date).

region.text: Thăng Long, empty when Toghon entered

ledger.note: 1285: the Yuan take Thăng Long. 'Yuan troops crossed the Nam Quan Pass on 27 January 1285'; in late February a Yuan fleet 'captured Thang Long and drove king Nhân Tông to the sea'.

region.text: Thăng Long

ledger.note: 9 June 1285: 'Mongol troops evacuated Thăng Long to withdraw to China' after the decisive Trần victory at Chương Dương.

region.text: Thăng Long

ledger.note: February 1288: Toghon's Yuan army returns to Thăng Long. The Yuan were 'successful in the early phases of the invasion, occupying and looting the Đại Việt capital'.

region.text: Thăng Long

ledger.note: 1288: the Yuan 'retreated from Thăng Long to their fortified main base in Vạn Kiếp on 5 March 1288'; their fleet was destroyed at Bạch Đằng in April 1288. Afterwards Đại Việt and Champa 'decided to accept the nominal supremacy of the Yuan dynasty and became tributary states' (the Yuan dossier carries the tint).

region.text: the Cham prefectures of Ô and Lý, renamed Thuận and Hóa (Thuận Hóa)

ledger.note: 1306: Chế Mân cedes Ô and Lý for Princess Huyền Trân. 'In 1306, the king of Champa, Chế Mân, offered Vietnam two Cham prefectures, Ô and Lý' in exchange for 'a marriage with the Vietnamese princess Huyền Trân'; Anh Tông renamed them Thuận and Hóa. The page gives no modern provinces; Thừa Thiên - Huế and Quảng Trị are read as in the champa dossier. Cliopatria moves the border in 1314.

region.text: Champa after the capture of Chế Chí

ledger.note: 1312: Trần Anh Tông defeats Champa and sets up its king. Anh Tông 'commanded three groups of Đại Việt military units to attack Champa in 1312'; 'Chế Chí was defeated and captured' and 'Anh Tông installed a hand-picked successor'. The page uses no word for vassal; the tint is a reading.

region.text: Champa

ledger.note: 1326: Champa wins back independence. Page silent: the Trần page does not cover 1326. The year is read from the champa dossier (se-01-a), which cites the Champa-Đại Việt War page for independence 'won back' in 1326; that page was not opened here.

region.text: the western upland part of the 1362 shape, outside the 1363 shape

ledger.note: 1363: the westernmost uplands leave the shape. Page silent: nothing on the Trần page; Cliopatria's shape loses 19,000 km2 on its western edge in the year its Lan Xang row begins, and the loss is bridged to lan-xang (gazetteer cell check: all 76 cells lost in 1363 lie inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape).

region.text: Hóa Châu, Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa, the zone of Chế Bồng Nga's raids (region as read in the champa dossier)

ledger.note: 1371: Chế Bồng Nga's Cham raids begin. The Champa page: Chế Bồng Nga 'launched six invasions of Dai Viet during the ... Champa-Đại Việt War (1367-1390)', sacking its capital 'in 1371, 1377, 1378, and 1383'. The Trần page adds the 1376 Vietnamese defeat at Đồ Bàn. The zone is read from the champa dossier; no border change ('no territorial changes').

region.text: Hóa Châu, Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa, the zone of Chế Bồng Nga's raids (region as read in the champa dossier)

ledger.note: 1390: Trần Khát Chân kills Chế Bồng Nga. 'In the first lunar month of 1390, Trần Khát Chân had a decisive victory over Champa'.
1397: the court leaves Thăng Long for Thanh Hóa. Infobox 'Thăng Long (1225-1397) Thanh Hóa (temp) (1397-1400)'; the Hồ page: Hồ Quý Ly 'had a new capital built, called Tây Đô (Western Capital)'.

1400: Hồ Quý Ly deposes the Trần and founds the Hồ dynasty (Đại Ngu). 'The end of the Trần dynasty came on the 28th day of the second lunar month (Gregorian: March 23) 1400' (Trần page); Hồ page: Hồ Quý Ly 'deposed him in 1400 and declared himself to be the new emperor'.

region.text: the 'large territory' ceded by Champa (the four regions Thăng, Hoa, Tư and Nghĩa in the champa dossier)

ledger.note: 1402: Hồ Hán Thương's army forces Champa to cede 'large territory'. 'In 1402 the army of the Hồ dynasty under general Đỗ Mãn made significant inroads against Champa, prompting the Champa king to cede large territory to Vietnam.' The page names no land; Quảng Nam, Đà Nẵng and Quảng Ngãi are read from the champa dossier.

region.text: the four regions ceded in 1402

ledger.note: 1406: the land ceded in 1402 returns to Champa. Page silent: the Hồ page does not mention it; the year and the return are read from the champa dossier (Champa-Đại Việt War page: 'Four former territories gained by Hồ Hán Thương were returned to Champa').

region.text: the Red River plain and the approaches from Lạng Sơn, where the Hồ were defeated at Moc Pham Giang and Ham Tu

ledger.note: 11 May 1406: the Ming invade. 'On 11 May 1406, the Yongle Emperor sent two forces for an invasion.' The page names no zone; the delta and the road from Lạng Sơn are read.

region.text: the Red River plain

ledger.note: 1407: the Hồ are defeated. 'The Hồ dynasty was conquered by the Chinese Ming dynasty in 1407.'

region.text: the whole Hồ state, in Cliopatria's last shape

ledger.note: 1407: the Ming take all of Đại Ngu and rule it as the Fourth Era of Northern Domination (Jiaozhi). 'The Hồ dynasty was conquered by the Chinese Ming dynasty in 1407.'

region.text: the Hồ state

ledger.note: 1407: the Hồ dynasty falls to the Ming and Đại Việt is absorbed as the Ming province of Jiaozhi (infobox 'Disestablished: 1407', succeeded by the 'Fourth Era of Northern Domination'). Cliopatria's row ends 1406 and its Ming shape grows in 1407.

wars.name: Song-Đại Cồ Việt war of 980-981
wars.outcome: The Song invasion ordered by Taizong in 980 was halted at Bạch Đằng in 981 and ended in peace talks; the Song accepted Lê Hoàn as military governor.
wars.note: 'Lê forces were successful at halting the overland advance of the Song forces'. No ground changed hands.

wars.name: Lê Hoàn's invasion of Champa
wars.outcome: Indrapura sacked and the Cham king killed in 982; the new king agreed to be a vassal in 983.
wars.note: The page also says the seized territory was 'merged into the country' without naming it.

wars.name: Lý Thánh Tông's invasion of Champa

zones.text: Địa Lí, Ma Linh and Bố Chính

wars.outcome: Rudravarman III captured; Địa Lí, Ma Linh and Bố Chính ceded and the tributary system restored.
wars.note: The page dates the campaign after Champa stopped paying tribute.

wars.name: Suryavarman II's wars against Đại Việt
wars.outcome: A Khmer army of 20,000 was routed at Nghệ An in 1128; with Cham help the Khmer briefly took Nghệ An in 1132; a Vietnamese counterattack in 1136 and the Cham peace ended the effort; no land changed hands.
wars.note: Tribute demanded of Lý Dương Hoán in 1127 and refused.

wars.name: Lý-Song War
wars.outcome: Lý forces took Qinzhou, Lianzhou and Yongzhou (1075-1076); the Song invasion of 1076-77 was stopped at the Như Nguyệt River; the Song kept Quảng Nguyên until a 1082 exchange returned it for the three prefectures; the 1084 talks fixed the frontier.
wars.note: Fighting 1075-1077; the exchange 1082; the border talks 6 July to 8 August 1084.

wars.name: First Mongol invasion of Đại Việt
wars.outcome: The Mongols took Thăng Long and left after nine days; Trần Thái Tông returned and a tributary relationship began.
wars.note: The Trần page dates the invasion 1257 in the text and 1258 in the infobox.

wars.name: Second Mongol invasion of Đại Việt
wars.outcome: Toghon crossed on 27 January, took Thăng Long in late February and withdrew on 9 June 1285; Sogetu's column came up through Nghệ An.
wars.note: The Yuan landed in Champa in February 1283 (champa dossier) and asked passage through Đại Việt in 1284.

wars.name: Third Mongol invasion of Đại Việt
wars.outcome: The Yuan occupied Thăng Long in February 1288, withdrew to Vạn Kiếp on 5 March and lost their fleet at Bạch Đằng in April; both Đại Việt and Champa accepted nominal Yuan supremacy.
wars.note: Invasion launched in the third lunar month of 1287 (Trần page).

wars.name: Trần campaign against Champa of 1312
wars.outcome: Three Vietnamese columns defeated and captured Chế Chí; Anh Tông installed a successor; relations 'remained strained'.
wars.note: No border change after the 1306 cession.

wars.name: Champa-Đại Việt War (1367-1390)

zones.text: Hóa Châu, Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa, the zone of Chế Bồng Nga's raids (region as read in the champa dossier)

wars.outcome: Chế Bồng Nga sacked Thăng Long in 1371, 1377, 1378 and 1383; a 1376 Vietnamese campaign was beaten at Đồ Bàn; Chế Bồng Nga was killed in the first lunar month of 1390. No territorial change.
wars.note: Dates from the Champa page; the Trần page gives 1376 and 1390 and no year for the assault on Thăng Long.

wars.name: Hồ invasion of Champa of 1402
wars.outcome: Champa ceded large territory to Đại Ngu.
wars.note: The land returned to Champa in 1406 (champa dossier).

wars.name: Ming conquest of Đại Ngu
wars.outcome: The Ming invaded on 11 May 1406 and conquered the Hồ in 1407.
wars.note: Hồ forces ambushed an early Ming force and the ambassador in April 1406; later defeats at Moc Pham Giang and Ham Tu 'precipitated the fall of the Hồ dynasty'.

certainty.note: Delta and Thanh-Nghệ are firm; the uplands to the Chinese frontier and the Champa march are claimed, not surveyed.

The Quảng Nguyên-Guihua frontier fixed in the 1084 talks 'exists largely unmodified to the present day' and is the one sharp border; the Champa frontier (Hải Vân line from 1306) and the western uplands are approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Ngô Dynasty' row (947-1406, 17 shapes) is one state under six dynasties (Ngô 939-968, Đinh 968-980, Anterior Lê 980-1009, Lý 1009-1225, Trần 1225-1400, Hồ 1400-1407); kept as one dossier with rename events (rule 2). The display name is not 'Ngô dynasty' because that would mislabel eight centuries; the slug and Wikipedia title are Cliopatria's. Later Vietnamese rows (Lê Dynasty 1429-, Mạc/Đại Việt, Trịnh and Nguyễn lords) are other dossiers; the Ming years 1407-1427 belong to ming-dynasty (Jiaozhi) with the Later Trần revolt unwritten.
Page budget (9 pages) spent, plus a tenth page (Khmer-Cham wars) opened so that the 1132-1136 Nghệ An contest matches the khmer-empire dossier. No page gave an area, so the area check was impossible; shape areas stand as Cliopatria's. Unverified within the budget: the 970 upland expansion (62k to 135k km2), the 1056 and 1188-1385 boundary noise, and the 1363 western loss (bridged at confidence 1 to lan-xang).
Page silent / bridged at confidence 1: 989 (end of the Indrapura occupation, from the champa dossier), 1069 (end of the first Cham vassalage), 1326 (end of the Trần tint, from the champa dossier), 1363, 1406 (return of the 1402 land). The Khmer-Cham wars page says the 1069 provinces were 'probably returned to Cham influence' in 1131-1136; no other page does and the shape is kept to 1187. Disagreements: Trần page 1257 (text) vs 1258 (infobox) for the first Mongol invasion; Lý-Song War page: five regions kept in 1077 against four prefectures and a county relinquished in 1082; Lý page dates the Trần takeover 1225 and 1226 in different passages; Hồ page lists the successor as 'Fourth Era of Northern Domination' while its body is silent. End year: identity.end is the page's 1407 while Cliopatria's last shape is 1406 and its Ming shape grows in 1407.
Suzerainty is carried by the suzerains: northern-song needs vassal events over this state (tribute from 972, Lê Hoàn as Annan duhu 986, Giao Chi Quan Vuong 993, Lý Nhân Tông 'King of Nam Bình' after 1077); mongol-empire/yuan-dynasty need the tribute from 1258/1288; ming-dynasty needs the 1407 gain. Not drawn: the twelve-warlords anarchy 965-968 (no dossier), the Ai Lao and Ngưu Hống uplands (page silent), and the Ngô rump after 944 (page silent).
